items.summary: Sunnycode v1 provides an open-access computational framework and reproducibility package supporting the research article Failure-Aware Gateway Placement and Road-Constrained Backbone Optimization for Resilient Urban LoRaWAN Networks , submitted to Digital Communications and Networks. The framework integrates OpenStreetMap (OSM) building-level sensing demand, radio-frequency (RF) feasibility, capacity-aware gateway assignment, worst-case single-gateway failure retention (N−1), gateway-load fairness, and road-constrained Steiner backbone synthesis. The repository includes Python implementations of the proposed optimization approach and four independent benchmark methods (Genetic Algorithm, Particle Swarm Optimization, Greedy, and Random Search). Dataset and experimental scope The computational experiment considers 685 building-level sensor anchors, 169 road vertices, 195 street edges, and 89 gateway candidates. The Full benchmark comprises 4,000 run-level observations obtained from 100 repetitions for each combination of five optimization methods and eight gateway budgets (k = 3–10). Repository contents Python source code and computational validation utilities. Nine original CSV files containing experimental observations, aggregated statistics, evaluation effort, and optimizer provenance. OpenStreetMap territorial input ( sunny3.osm ). Forty scientific figures in PDF format. Installation and execution instructions using Anaconda. SHA-256 file-integrity manifest and licensing information. The archived results support independent verification of the reported statistics and new computational experiments. The original historical environment metadata and detailed event histories are not included; therefore, bit-for-bit replay of the historical execution environment is not claimed. Scientific scope: RF coverage and packet delivery ratio are model-derived planning estimates rather than field-calibrated measurements. N−1 resilience represents gateway-access service retention and does not certify fault-tolerant physical-backbone connectivity. This software and dataset are released to support transparent computational research, independent assessment, and further development of resilient urban Internet of Things infrastructure planning.
items.title: Sunnycode v1 A Reproducible Framework for Failure-Aware Gateway Placement and Road-Constrained Backbone Optimization in Urban LoRaWAN Networks

items.summary: This Zenodo record is a permanently preserved version of a PREreview. You can view the complete PREreview at https://prereview.org/reviews/23121295 . This narrative review asks how psychosexual rehabilitation after cancer can be delivered at scale, rather than describing how common sexual dysfunction is. The author organizes the intervention evidence by intensity of care. Low-intensity measures (structured discussion, lubricants and moisturizers, topical lidocaine, brief clinician training) are cheap and reasonably supported. Two widely recommended physical interventions have weaker evidence than assumed: scheduled PDE5 inhibitor "penile rehabilitation" and routine vaginal dilation during radiotherapy. Psychological interventions show small pooled effects, but moderate effects in targeted trials, most clearly therapist-guided internet-based CBT in breast cancer. From this the author proposes a five-step stepped-care model (Steps 0–4, built on extended PLISSIT) with explicit criteria for stepping up and down, plus adaptations for AYA, men on ADT, and sexual and gender minority survivors. The paper moves the field forward by reframing the problem as one of delivery, by challenging two entrenched practices, and by turning scattered evidence into a model that oncology teams, including nurses, could adopt and test. Major issues Methods are not reproducible. The review relies on "targeted searches" with no databases, dates, search terms, or selection process described. Evidence is "appraised qualitatively" with no tool such as GRADE or risk-of-bias assessment. Claims like "strongest trial evidence in breast cancer" may reflect selective sampling. The stepped-care model is not empirically validated. It was derived by the author "mapping" interventions to levels of care, with no consensus process, stakeholder input, or implementation data. The 8–12 week step-up threshold has no cited support. The conclusion that evidence "supports matching intensity to need" goes beyond what the cited studies tested, since none compared stepped care with usual care or direct referral (the paper admits this only at the end). Evidence for Steps 0–2 is mostly clinician-level, not patient-level. The cited training studies show clinicians discuss sexuality more often, not that patient outcomes improve. Yet these steps form the base of the model. Feasibility of nurse- or clinician-delivered care also rests largely on one HSCT trial. Key claims rest on weak or non-peer-reviewed sources. The HSCT multimodal trial [34] is a conference abstract that is called "important for the model." Other supports [28, 47] are also abstracts. Pilot RCTs (23 and 29 couples) underpin the "medium-to-large" couple therapy claims. The paper applies evidence standards inconsistently. It criticizes penile rehabilitation and during-radiotherapy dilation for weak evidence, then recommends supported dilation after radiotherapy based on observational data and an uncontrolled 53-woman cohort (11.5% to 60.9% pre-post), and cites a regimen from an abstract [28]. Inference from pooled versus targeted effects is speculative. The difference (SMD 0.24 vs. d 0.43–0.72) is taken to show that interventions work best when targeted, which supports stepped care. It could equally reflect heterogeneity, study quality, outcome measures, or small-study effects. Effect sizes of different metrics are also compared without confidence intervals. There is no limitations section. It should cover search bias, the breast-cancer skew, scarce data for men, SGM, and LMIC settings, and the lack of cost and workforce evidence. Minor issues PLISSIT is never spelled out, and AYA HOPE is not defined. "Psychosexual rehabilitation" is defined as a staged process but used loosely to include medical and physical treatments.
